Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS

Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member

描述一次你为家人感到骄傲的时刻

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member

  • When it happened (这件事发生在什么时候)
  • Who the person is (这个人是谁)
  • What the person did (这个人做了什么)
  • And explain why you felt proud of him/her (并解释为什么你为他/她感到骄傲)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a time when you felt proud of a family member

I'd like to talk about a moment when I felt really proud of my younger brother. It happened last summer, when the results of his final exams came out, the big national exam that decides which university you get into. I remember sitting at home with my parents, all of us waiting nervously for the results to be released online. My brother is two years younger than me, and honestly, he's always been the quieter one in the family. He never boasted about his studies, so we had no idea how well he had prepared. When the results finally appeared, he had scored far above the top-tier university line, which was way beyond what any of us expected. My parents were overjoyed, and my mum actually called all her relatives to share the news. The reason I felt so proud of him is that I knew how much effort he had put in. For the whole year, he got up at six every morning to study, and he gave up most of his weekends. What struck me most was his calmness, because he never once complained about the pressure. To be honest, I also felt a little envious, because I wished my own scores had been as good as his. But mostly, I was genuinely proud, and I told him so that evening. Looking back, it's a moment I won't forget, because it showed me what quiet determination can achieve.

去年夏天弟弟高考出分，远超一本线，全家惊喜；他一年来每天六点起床学习、放弃周末，从不抱怨，我既骄傲又有点羡慕，希望自己分数也那么高。

Q2When would parents feel proud of their children?

Generally speaking, parents feel proud when their children achieve something meaningful, like doing well in exams, winning a competition or showing kindness to others. In my country, academic success is probably the most common source of pride, because education is seen as the key to a better future. That said, I think parents feel even prouder when their children become independent and responsible, because that shows the values they taught have really taken root.

父母在孩子取得成就时骄傲，如考试好、获奖、善良；我国最看重学业成功，但孩子独立负责更让父母自豪。

Q3Should parents reward children? Why and how?

I'd say yes, rewards can be helpful, but they need to be used sensibly. The main reason is that rewards give children a clear sense of achievement and encourage them to keep trying. However, I think the reward should be more about recognition than money, like extra family time or a favourite meal, so that children learn to value effort rather than just the prize.

奖励有用但要适度；奖励给孩子成就感、鼓励坚持，但应重认可而非金钱，如家庭时间或喜欢的饭菜，让孩子重视努力本身。

Q4Is it good to reward children too often? Why?

Not really, I don't think so. If children are rewarded too often, they may start to expect a prize for everything they do, and they might lose their inner motivation. Having said that, occasional rewards are fine, as long as they are linked to real effort, because the goal is to build good habits, not to create a habit of bargaining.

频繁奖励不好；孩子会期待事事有奖、失去内在动力，可能没奖励就不做事；偶尔奖励且与真实努力挂钩才合适。

Q5On what occasions would adults be proud of themselves?

I think adults feel proud of themselves when they overcome a real challenge, like getting a promotion, buying their first home or completing a difficult project. These moments matter because they represent years of effort. In my country, many adults also feel proud when they can support their parents financially, since that is seen as a sign of maturity. On the whole, I'd say pride for adults usually comes from achievements that prove their independence and capability.

成年人克服真正挑战时自豪，如升职、买房、完成难项目；我国很多人以能赡养父母为傲，骄傲多来自证明独立与能力。

Q6Do rewards help a child become better?

To some extent, yes, they do. Rewards can encourage a child to repeat good behaviour, especially in the early years, when children are still learning what is right and wrong. For example, praising a child for sharing toys can make sharing a habit. However, I believe long-term improvement depends more on internal motivation, like curiosity and a sense of responsibility. So rewards are a useful starting point, but they shouldn't be the only reason a child behaves well.

奖励有一定帮助，能鼓励孩子重复好行为；但长期进步更靠内在动力如好奇心和责任感，奖励只是起点。

Q7Do you think choosing a college major is closely related to a future career?

I'd say it's related, but not as closely as people often think. In my country, many graduates end up working in fields completely different from their major, because the job market changes quickly. For example, a friend of mine studied history but now works in marketing. Having said that, certain majors, like medicine or engineering, do lead directly to specific careers. So on the whole, a major opens doors, but it doesn't lock you into one path.

专业与职业有关联但没那么紧密；我国很多毕业生转行，如学历史做营销；但医学、工程等专业直接对应职业，专业开门但不锁死道路。
